column1: DENGUE CASE REPORTING During  the  33rd  week,  2628  suspected  dengue  cases were reported across all 26 districts, compared to 3254 cases in the previous week, reflecting 19.2% decrease. The  Western  Province  accounted  for  53.1%  of  total cases,  with the  Colombo  Municipal  Council (CMC) contributing 3.1%, the rest of Colombo District 20.6%, Gampaha  District  23.1%,  and  Kalutara  District  6.4%. Outside the Western Province, notable case contributions were reported from Kandy (10.4%), Galle (4.6%),  Kegalle (4.1%),  Matara (3.5%),  Ratnapura (3.3%),  Badulla  (2.6%),  Kurunegala  (2.6%),  Puttalam (2.5%), and Kalmunai (2.2%) (see Table 1) (compared to the  previous  week,  colour  of  %:  red=increase,  green=decrease, blue=no change). WEEKLY DISTRIBUTION OF DENGUE PATIENTS in 2024, 2025 and 2026    Source: NaDSys – National Dengue Surveillance System HIGH RISK MOH AREAS  As presented in Table 2, during the 33rd week of 2026, 76 Medical Officer of Health (MOH) areas were identified as high-risk, including 5 newly flagged areas (highlighted in light red in Table 2). Previously classified 25 high-risk MOH areas in week 32, were not identified as high-risk in the 33rd week of 2026 (Table 2). MIDNIGHT TOTAL OF DENGUE PATIENT ADMISSIONS *  After  incorporating  delayed  hospital  reports,  the average midnight total for the 32nd week increased from 1133 to 1137. In the 33rd week of 2026, the average midnight total of dengue  patients  across  78  sentinel  hospitals  was  809. Compared  to  the  previous  week,  in  the  33rd  week,  12 hospitals  reported  an increase,  while  47  reported  a decrease.
